handlers.comment: E-stop over UART, as the CAN E-stop frame: the E-stop error is latched, the motor is released and a calibration that is running ends (#Idle does not end one). #Clear clears it. Until 2026-11 only CAN could do this; a host on UART had to reset the drive to stop a calibration.
handlers.name: Estop

handlers.comment: Enter calibration mode #Cal: the calibration, then always the encoder table and the anti-cogging, then save; #Calonly: the calibration alone
handlers.name: Cal

handlers.comment: Enter calibration mode #Cal: the calibration, then always the encoder table and the anti-cogging, then save; #Calonly: the calibration alone
handlers.name: Calonly
handlers.response: Cal: not started, the E-stop is latched (#Clear first)

handlers.comment: Enter calibration mode fro angle offset
handlers.name: Calangle
handlers.response: Calangle: not started, the drive is in error (#Error, #Clear)

handlers.comment: set get Iqoffset that will be used to search angle offset
handlers.name: Iqoffset

handlers.name: Ilim

handlers.comment: Enable/disable termistor mesurement 0 is off, 1 is on
handlers.name: Term

handlers.comment: Print if there are any errors
handlers.name: Error

handlers.comment: Clear All errors and set mode to IDLE Will not clear calibration error. If motor is not calibrated you will need to set controller.Calibrated to 1. with #Calibrated 1 command
handlers.name: Clear

handlers.comment: Enter closed loop mode, idle state #Close while a calibration runs: end it the way an E-stop or its own failure does (its steps start over next time, the current and voltage limits are put back, the bridge is off). Taking the interrupt away from it, as #Close does below, left it half-done: the next #Cal went on from the old step and the calibration's 1600 mA limit could be saved.
handlers.name: Close

handlers.name: gosteps

handlers.comment: Print a summary of available commands
handlers.name: Help

handlers.comment: Print Information about motor driver and motor
handlers.name: Info

handlers.comment: Set/get the tool id: what this drive is built into (0 none, 1 SSG-48, 11-33 MSG with tens = rail 1/2/3 = 100/150/200 mm and units = stepper 1/2/3 = 21.5/40/60 mm, 200-254 custom). Saved with #Save.
handlers.name: Tool

handlers.comment: The encoder table on the drive (encal.h): #Encal measures it (one shaft turn each way at 2048 ticks/s, about 20 s; the shaft must be free), #Encal save also saves, #Encal all also identifies the anti-cogging and saves both, #Encal stop aborts, #Encal on / off switches the correction, #Encal state shows it. A tone through the motor (batch 22): #Tone f,mA[,ms] (ms left out: 500; 0: until #Tone off); #Tone off. It plays while the drive holds or moves; from idle the drive first holds the position it is at.
handlers.name: Tone

handlers.comment: Any CAN parameter by number (batch 20): #Par lists all, #Par n reads one, #Par n,v sets it
handlers.name: Par

handlers.comment: On-drive anti-cogging identification (cogcal.h): #Cogcal runs it, #Cogcal save also saves, #Cogcal stop aborts, #Cogcal state shows it. One motor turn each way at the cogcal speed: the shaft must be free to turn.
handlers.name: Cogcal

handlers.comment: Product lock: #Product shows the board's stamp; #Product claim stamps it as this product (a motor the rule misjudges, a repaired board); #Product clear removes the stamp. UART only, on purpose.
handlers.name: Product
handlers.response: Board stamped as this product. Power-cycle the drive.

handlers.comment: Set/get the watchdog fallback: #WdFb time_ms,current_mA,speed_ticks_s,after_action (after_action 0 legacy, 2 brake, 3 coast). Used by watchdog actions 1 (hold) and 4 (descend). Saved with #Save.
handlers.name: WdFb

handlers.comment: Set/Get gripper position setpoint and go to gripper mode (goto action big)
handlers.name: Grippos

handlers.comment: Print all currently set PID parameters for every control mode
handlers.name: Param

handlers.comment: Periodically send messages without request from host. Messeges are position, speed and Iq current. Format of the command is #Cyc time. Time is variable in millisecond (needs to be integer) If time is not given (or 0) command is disabled. Format of cyclic output is: $Position Speed Torque\n Cyclic can also be used with: https://github.com/nathandunk/BetterSerialPlotter
handlers.name: Cyc

handlers.comment: Periodically send messages without request from host. Messeges are position, speed and Iq current. Format of the command is #Cyca time. Time is variable in millisecond (needs to be integer) If time is not given (or 0) command is disabled. Format of cyclic output is: $,Position,Speed,Torque\n Cyca can be used with arduino plotter
handlers.name: Cyca
